components.gap: The success condition needs each claimed stopping/error guarantee to be shown, by written steps, to hold for the actual stopping procedure. Five guarantees have one case discharged by 'similarly' or 'the same argument' instead: (1) thm:p15-se-deadline, the P_1 bound P_1(T<=N) >= P_1(Z_N>=a), 'by the same argument' (annex 418-419); (2) thm:p15-se-lattice, the upper terminal support a_0..a_0+g_2-1 behind the exact exit probabilities and gamma, 'follows similarly' (annex 195-196); (3) thm:p15-se-truncation, the alternative-error bound beta_N <= beta' + P_1(b<Z_N<=0), a one-sentence pointer without the coupling and union-bound steps that are written for the null half (annex 437-439), although the held source writes both halves at (4.63)-(4.66), printed p.153; (4) thm:p15-se-binomial, the eta constant used in the operating-characteristic bounds, 'similarly' (annex 260-261); (5) thm:p15-se-transform, the r<0 integrability case, 'in the same calculation' (annex 343-344). Under the audit rule these proofs are partial. Every other stopping/error proof on the route is written in full: termination, coupled error inequalities, the dependent-density version, nominal boundaries, operating-characteristic bounds, the absorption recursion, repeated independent looks and all results of the w02b-p15-061 chapter.

The text says looks at n,2n,...,Kn 'therefore have the same joint law for every n', inferring this from the covariance formula alone. Under the general i.i.d. hypotheses of the preceding lemma, only the covariances are shown to be independent of n. The joint-law statement is established only in the Gaussian null model.

The method cites Wald eqs (4.36)-(4.52), but beyond 'Derivatives at real tau=0 give moments' it does not present the conditional-moment equations (4.46)-(4.50) (printed pp.149-150). It states the one-sided continuous approximation only for positive drift, omitting the source's B>0, A=infinity, Ez<0 case (printed p.150). It also omits the remark that h=1 under H0 and h=-1 under H1 (printed p.135). Recorded for the user's scope decision; not used for the C04 verdict.

The source's dependent-observation example (normal autoregressive joint density, printed p.130) is not reproduced. Termination for dependent processes is assumed as a hypothesis, which is consistent with the source asserting it only 'under very general conditions'.

The treatment states its source scope as Part I, Sections 2-4. Part II (Sections 5-6, printed pp.158-186: one-sided and composite alternatives) is outside it, and no rationale is given for the extent. Whether Part II falls under the queue's 'selected test construction' is a scope question for the user.
